fixes.explanation: I see why that sounds nice, friend. But the LORD says the opposite: "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua, Israel's leader, is old and well along in years, and there's still plenty left to take. Picture opening the oven door, ready to call it a day, and finding three more batches of dough waiting for you.

False is right, baker! The text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day." (Joshua 13:13) Just before that, Moses, Israel's leader, had struck down Og's kingdom and dispossessed them (Joshua 13:12). Then this verse turns and says these two peoples were not driven out. I think that's a detail worth holding onto.

Yes, baker! Levi is the tribe set apart to carry the ark and serve the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:8), and Moses gave them no land. Their inheritance is this: "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) A few verses later it's said again: "The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:33) Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh got territory from Moses, and Levi got a promise instead. I think that's worth a second look.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
Calling this the one spot where the work of driving people out was unfinished goes beyond the text. The chapter also describes other land that remained to be possessed.
The comparison likens the Geshurites and Maacathites to crumbs that need to be swept away, putting down those peoples.
The statement that Levi was set apart to serve the LORD is not stated in this passage and needs a reference, such as Deuteronomy 10:8.

Saying every other tribe got a map with borders suggests all the other tribal portions had already been assigned. In this chapter, Joshua is told to divide the land among the nine tribes and half-tribe of Manasseh.
